newsitem.title: USA: Jury selection starts in Miami drug lawyer trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury selection starts in Miami drug lawyer trial.

text.p: Jury selection began on Monday in the trial of six people charged with illegally assisting Colombia's Cali drug cartel, among them a former top Justice Department official and a former U.S. prosecutor.

The six were among 59 mentioned in a sweeping 208-page indictment unsealed in June 1995, the result of nearly four years of investigation that federal officials said uncovered shipments of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of cocaine into the United States.
Prosecutors called the indictment the "most significant drug trafficking indictment of the Cali cartel in U.S. history."

The best-known of the defendants in the trial that began on Monday before U.S. District Judge William Hoeveler was Michael Abbell, who was chief of the U.S. Justice Department's Office of International Affairs during President Ronald Reagan's administration.

The defendants also included William Moran, a criminal defence attorney and former prosecutor, and four men U.S. officials charge helped warehouse and ship drugs -- Luis Grajales, Eddie Martinez, Ramon Martinez and Jose Herrera Solas.

Attorneys said it could take a week to seat a 12-member jury for a trial expected to last anywhere from three to six months. Court officials said some 850 questionnaires had been distributed to potential jurors.

The lawyers were charged, among other things, with inventing false evidence to help protect drug kingpins, and providing payments to help support the families of drug traffickers arrested in the United States.

U.S. authorities said those indicted were major figures in the Cali cartel responsible for more than 440,000 pounds (200,000 kg) of cocaine, or up to 80 percent of the cocain imported into the United States between 1984 and the unsealing of the indictment.
At least four other attorneys named in the indictment have reached plea agreements and were expected to take the stand once testimony began.
